transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Um… I’m probably making a bigger deal of it than it is, but EAP suggested I talk to someone. Lately at work, little sudden noises—like a file drawer slamming or someone dropping a coffee mug—make me jump really hard. My chest starts racing, and it takes longer than it should to calm down. It’s kind of embarrassing, honestly.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about these reactions happening again, especially in situations where you might be caught off guard by a noise?

Yeah… I guess I do, a little. I try not to make it a whole thing, but what made me call EAP was that every little bang in the office—like a file drawer shutting or someone dropping a coffee mug—makes me jump really hard. Then my chest keeps racing way longer than it should. So I do catch myself kind of bracing for it, if that makes sense.
Have you found yourself avoiding certain places or situations at work because you're worried about being startled by a noise?

I don’t think I’ve really been avoiding places, no. I mean, I might choose a quieter spot if I have the option, but I’m still going where I need to go at work. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.
Outside of the loud or sudden noises at work, do you find yourself feeling unusually alert or on edge in other situations, like you’re always watching for something bad to happen?

I mean… not all the time, I don’t think. But in the office lately, yeah, I do catch myself kind of scanning more than I used to. Like I’ll check where my boss is, where the exits are, or whether someone’s coming up behind me, even when I’m supposed to be focused on my team.

It sounds a little dramatic when I say it out loud, but it’s just… I notice I’m doing it.
Have you ever had an experience that was really traumatic or scary, where you felt like you were reliving it when something reminded you of it?

I don’t think so… not like reliving something, exactly. I’ve definitely been jumpy with reminders, like the noises, but I wouldn’t say I’m back in some moment or seeing it happen again.

I mean, unless I’m misunderstanding what you mean by reliving it. But no, nothing like a full flashback or anything like that.
Have you ever had intrusive thoughts or memories about a specific stressful or traumatic event that keeps coming back, even when you don’t want to think about it?

Not really, no. I mean, I’ll think about how tense I’ve been or replay little work moments in my head, but I don’t have one specific event that keeps forcing its way back or anything like that.

At least, not that I’ve noticed. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you noticed yourself feeling more negative or down lately, like you’re stuck in a bad mood or seeing the world more negatively than before?

Yeah… maybe a little. I wouldn’t say I’m, like, miserable all the time or anything. I’m still doing normal stuff — I still go to beach volleyball, and I made dinner for a couple friends last weekend.

But honestly, it kind of feels like I’m just going through the motions. Like I’m there, I’m doing it, I can talk and laugh if I’m supposed to, but it doesn’t really land as fun or satisfying the way it normally would. I don’t know if that counts as “down,” exactly, but it’s different for me.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying the things you used to, like activities or time with friends, even though you’re still doing them?

Yeah… I guess that’s probably the best way to put it. I’m still doing the things — like I still show up for beach volleyball, and I had a couple friends over for dinner last weekend — so it’s not like I’ve stopped my life or anything.

But it feels kind of… flat, I guess. Like I’m there and I’m participating, but it doesn’t really feel fun or satisfying the way it normally would. More like I’m going through the motions. Does that make sense?
Has this lack of enjoyment or flat feeling been happening most days, and does it seem to last for the whole day, even when you’re not at work?

Yeah… I think it’s been most days, if I’m being honest. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is — I’m still doing things, like volleyball and having friends over — but even outside work it’s kind of there.

Not necessarily every second of the day, but a lot of the time it feels like I’m just going through the motions, and the fun parts don’t really hit the way they usually would. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, even when you’re doing them?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, because I am still doing the stuff. I still go to beach volleyball, and I had a couple friends over for dinner last weekend.

It’s just… it doesn’t feel the same. Like I’m there and I’m doing what I normally do, but it feels more like I’m checking the box than actually enjoying it. The fun part doesn’t really land, if that makes sense.
Can you think of any specific event or period in your life that felt really stressful or overwhelming, even if it didn’t seem like a big deal to others at the time?

I’m not sure I can point to one specific thing, honestly. I mean, everyone has stressful periods, right? Work gets heavy sometimes, life stuff piles up, but I don’t know if there’s one event I’d call… overwhelming.

Maybe I’m not thinking about it the right way. Are you asking about something major-major, or just anything that felt like too much at the time?
Have you had days where you felt down or hopeless, or where things just didn’t seem worth the effort, even if only for a few hours at a time?

I don’t know… maybe a little here and there, but I wouldn’t say hopeless exactly. More like some days things feel heavier than they should, or it takes more effort to get myself moving.

It’s not like I’m sitting there all day thinking nothing matters or anything. Just… for a few hours sometimes, I’ll feel kind of low and think, “Do I really have to deal with this right now?” But I can usually push through it. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you felt little interest or pleasure in doing things most of the time, even when you’re not at work?

Yeah… I guess so, but I’m still doing things, so I don’t want it to sound like I’ve completely stopped living or anything.

Like I still go to beach volleyball, and I did make dinner for a couple friends last weekend. It’s just… when I’m actually there, it feels kind of like I’m going through the motions. The part that’s supposed to feel fun or satisfying doesn’t really land the way it used to. Does that make sense?
Have you felt more fatigued or low on energy lately, even when you haven’t been doing anything particularly taxing?

I don’t think so… not in a way I’ve really noticed. I mean, I get tired like anyone else, especially after work or if I don’t sleep great, but I wouldn’t say I’m unusually wiped out when I haven’t done much.

Maybe I’m not paying close enough attention, but it doesn’t feel like a major thing for me. Is that okay to say?
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating or focusing lately, like it’s harder to think through problems or stay focused on tasks, even when you’re trying?

Yeah… a little. I mean, I’m still getting my work done, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But I have noticed I’ll open Salesforce to check my reps’ notes, and then I realize I’ve just been staring at the same account for like ten minutes and not really taking anything in. And even small decisions at work, like who should cover a client visit, feel harder to think through than they probably should.

It’s not constant, but it’s been happening enough that I’ve noticed it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, more days than not, even if only mildly?

I don’t think I’d say depressed most of the day, no. I mean… I’ve had moments where I feel kind of off or flat, but I’m not walking around crying or anything like that.

Maybe “down” is a little strong? I don’t know. I’m trying to answer it the right way. It’s more like I’m not totally myself sometimes, but I wouldn’t say it’s most of the day on most days.
Have you found it harder to make decisions or think clearly lately, even about small things at work or in your daily life?

Yeah… I guess I have noticed that, a bit. I don’t want to overstate it, because I’m still functioning at work.

But I’ll open Salesforce to look at my reps’ notes, and then realize I’ve just been staring at the same account for like ten minutes without really processing it. And even simple stuff, like deciding who should cover a client visit, feels harder than it normally would.

It’s not like I can’t make decisions at all, but it takes more effort than it should. Does that make sense?
Have you had days where you felt down or flat for most of the day, and if so, how often has that happened over the past couple of weeks?

I don’t think it’s been most of the day, honestly. Maybe I’ve had a few stretches where I felt kind of flat or not like myself, but it hasn’t been like an all-day thing.

Over the past couple weeks… I’m not totally sure how often. A handful of times maybe? But I wouldn’t want to say it’s been most days if that’s not accurate. Does that answer it the way you’re asking?
